reviews.text: What could be a decent game (preview) ruined by anti-player bias like enemies knowing where you are at all times, and an idiotic cutscene death (at least do it with a weapon that could actually deal more than 12 damage). Overall Points of (Un)Interest do nothing beside the first one, they're just combat, from which you can't recover, because there are no additional resting points, even the options that say "Rest" or "The villagers allowed you to rest" do nothing for either your Mech's health or your sanity (which is never explained and seems to do nothing so far).

The TL;DR version: if you can deal with irritating dialogue and broadly unlikeable characters, there's a lot here for someone who likes the Front Mission games. It's a big ask, though. I've had the demo for Kriegsfront Tactics installed pretty much since it initially came out. I've replayed the missions included in it at least a dozen times so far. As a fan of the Front Mission games and mech games in general, I've been counting the days to release on this one. If you haven't played the demos or aren't sure what the pitch is on Kriegsfront Tactics: it's a mech tactics game in the vein of the Front Mission series with a vaguely Vietnam war story theme. Your mechs have different loadouts and capabilities. Typically, you can move a little and shoot, but this is much closer to an action point economy (maybe along the lines of Jagged Alliance) than a more XCOM-style: you can move and shoot/use a special ability or sprint to cover more ground. Certain special abilities require more action points that might mean you don't want to move a mech, or only move them a square or two to get a better vantage point. You're most likely to encounter this with the sniper mechs, where you probably want to take aimed shots whenever possible (this brings up a first-person view where you can free-aim and see what the damage outcome might be depending on the part of the mech you're aiming for). As this is a mech game, you can blow limbs off to reduce the combat effectiveness of opposing mechs. So far, I haven't seen the Battletech-style option to go for headshots on opposing mechs and they all seem to at least have the option to just ram into you if you disable their other weapons. I think the art direction and presentation is excellent. The animations are snappy, the art direction is evocative of PSX-era tactics games. When pilots are talking, a portrait of them will pop up and those are pretty well-realized, too. This prologue is the devs starting to flesh out the RPG and story elements of the game from the demos (which were combat missions with minimal narrative setup). The opening cinematic does a great job of setting up the stakes for the world (a vaguely post-WWII narrative except there are mechs and after the defeat of a major power, those mechs were just left where they were due to a lack of logistical support, so they were reclaimed by regular people). After that, the storytelling gets pretty rough. It's tough to get a handle on the vernacular of the faction the player controls at the start. On the one hand, they're using common British slang, but seemed to be framed as US (or otherwise Western) forces. Everyone's calling each other a bloke, but the iconography on the mechs seems Americanized. It's not uncommon for the Front Mission games to mash various geopolitical entities together and come up with a new term for them, but if that was covered in the opening cinematic, it slipped right past me. I think the bigger problem is that a lot of folks on your squad are abrasive jerks. Given the clear cues the game takes from films set during the Vietnam war, my most charitable read is that at least one character is modelled after Sergeant Hartman from Full Metal Jacket, but without taking the time to really ease you in with a more reasonable main character (one is present, but needs more time to breathe before introducing someone as bracing as this game's version of Hartman). Another squad mate is saved at the end of a tutorial mission by a woman pilot and he spends at least two screens of dialogue explaining how much he thinks she's a ♥♥♥♥♥. It's possible the game is setting up an "are we the baddies" moment, but it could also be that the writing is just being abrasive in an attempt to signal how Adult its themes are (and instead conveying the absolute opposite). I think there's a way to do the character-driven exploration into the various weirdoes grappling with the erosion of their humanity and empathy as they fight an unjust and nightmarish war (that just so happens to feature a lot of big stompy robots). I think that's half the plot of at least two or three Gundams. I just don't think the moment-to-moment storytelling is up to the task as it sits right now. It's tough to land on a recommendation here. I think the tactical design and the general presentation of the mech combat is great. There's a lot of promise in the overall worldbuilding, but the dialogue was enough to sap a lot of the enthusiasm I'd had for the game by the time I was a couple missions deep. It's still probably an easier recommendation than the recent remasters of the Front Mission games (which, to be clear: I quite like, but the overall encounter design has not aged well at all in those games). Given the caveats I've had to put together here, I can't quite recommend it, but it's free - feel free to give it a shot and see how you feel.
Jan Cox

At its current state I can't recommend. This is a prologue/proof of concept so a lot could change moving forward and it needs to. Good: mech games are far and few between and this has potential to be a good one. Aesthetics are solid, sound is nice and crunchy with meaty sounding guns. You can customize your mechs and paint them. Bad: You have to spam spacebar to get through dialogue, and this gets tedious when you lose as you have to taptaptaptap to get through everything youve heard before. It needs a skip scene option. AI CHEATS. They always know where you are, and there are some very unfair fights. Not challenging, unfair. A full game will need a better skill ramp up, and the whole scavenging ammo / repair is annoying. It forces you to go into a tough fight with damaged mechs and low to no ammo because you had a bad fight before. That takes player choice out of the equation and punishes you for mistakes you made earlier but barely got through. Balancing is also bad, theres a set piece story battle and you're not only against more powerful mechs but they have equal numbers and you start getting shot by a hidden mech. At this point you've had a few fights yet the game acts puts you in this situation. Challenge is fine, being a jerk to your players even if unintentionally is not. Other: Its an Xcom Lite Mech game. With some tweaks and improvements this could be an excellent game and I hope it gets the improvements it needs for the full game.

I hate tactical games, so it's a huge shock for me to say that THIS IS THE BEST TACTICAL GAME I'VE EVER EXPERIENCED! Also, giant robots make everything better. My only problem is why the nation supposedly representing Indonesia is using the phrase 'Merdeka' repeatedly. 'Merdeka' is the Malay word for "independence" & is symbolic with the Independence Day of Malaysia from foreign rule, which is celebrated through "Hari Merdeka" ("Day of Independence") in Malaysia. Merdeka Day = National Day = Malaysia Day By the way, I'm typing this 3 days before Malaysia's 67th Merdeka Day (which takes place on 31st August 2024).

Very promising. I loved Front Mission. I love mechs. I love turn based combat. I especially love the character driven approach often missing in games like this. However lack of a normal save-load system is a deal breaker for me. And at least in the prologue, there seems to be no clear way to replenish weapons and repair your mechs. I do not at all enjoy this kind of restrictive approach towards gameplay. Add a save load system, and a better sandbox "overworld" with more options, characters, activities, freedom (ala BattleTech) and I will be happy to pay good price for the full game.

Can't currently recommend it. 1) Obviously an homage to Front Mission; very well done, good framing, nice graphics, etc. No complaints there. 2) Good gameplay; movement feels good, mechanics are easy to understand. 3) Way too punishing for things outside of my control. In my 3rd mission, 4 of my teammembers died to sniper fire from positions I had no way of knowing enemies could be. "Oh, but you can move in the trees!" I WAS IN THE TREES. I WAS IN COVER. Every sniper shot hit center mass and pretty much cored out any of my mechs that weren't at full health. When your mission balancing is "5 armored mechs vs 10 scrap mechs," it seems fine until you realize their guns do the same damage as yours; since armor is carried over between missions with no way to fix it (presumably there's a way later), it's basically attritional warfare where the enemy is infinite and your armor is not. I like it, but the tonal whiplash completely took me out of the experience.

I wasn't even going to leave a review, but this game deserves one - For it being just a Prologue, this game had no bugs, no issues, and best of all - It has that tactical feel to it that you would only get from games like Xcom, from Battletech to Menace; Yes, there's RNG, but it also has Line of Sight mechanics, high and lower grounds for verticality advantages and distance mechanics as well, so the further you are, the less damamge you do. The game has some simple but interesting mechs, single-handed and double-handed weapons, shields and some cool attachments for AOE bombardments as shoulder pads. Seems like the tip of the iceberg from what they've given us so far, so I'm really intrigued to see what's in store for the full release. The game also has a decent storyline going for it thus far, and I'm keen to see where it leads, feels like one of those American war movies without the mechs. Side note: As I mentioned before, I wasn't going to write a review, but it deserves one.. And for me to respond to a comment of a negative review that mentioned that "There seems to be no clear way to replenish weapons and repair your mechs". To the silly dingus who probably never got to the point of doing so, there is 1 station on the map to repair all your Mechs, once only (Due to it being a single run Prologue); And there are plenty of weapons to pick up along the way, I had aside in the stash about 6 different weapons I wasn't using.

Alright. Proper review time. Story? Very heavily inspired off of the Vietnam war and colonialism as a whole. Lore is your the big country (cough cough america or VOC) and your fighting against insurgents that have taken weapons from the country you just defeated to take this land because the people living on the land want to be free and not the battleground of war. Of course there's mechs involved and all that. At the end there's a pretty cool cutscene where it shows that both sides are relatively manipulative. Music: Music was catchy sounded nice to my ears and wasn't reptitive sounding just like your standard ambience. Sound: I personally very much enjoyed the sound design most favoured being the 'WHUMP WHUMP' sound after you fire off your shoulder mounted grenande launcher and do some extreme deforestation. Speaking of that. Gameplay: I played through the demo/prologue about 4 times now beating the final battle each time in different ways. And I have to say the cliche line "Easy to learn, Hard to master." Because well that's what it is. At first your gonna think some invulnurable invisible enemy is sniping you but no, its just a hidden enemy in the trees. You can do exactly what they're doing (with better effect hopefully.) Lets get down to business, its a turn based game so you have AP of course shooting requires the most AP moving requires the second least and most importantly evading (provided you are facing the enemy mech) is 0 AP, though it only has a 50% to trigger. you have specific parts on your mech that can be aimmed at and destroyed and vice versa for enemy mechs. Shoot the body? It has the most HP but once it goes down to 0 the mech explodes. Shoot the legs? Enemy can't dodge and takes 3x the AP to move. Shoot the Arms? Congrats you've turned the enemy mech into one of those rubber balls that hurt but are relatively unharmful unless you get pelted by like ten of them. The enemy only uses the 'fire weapon' command as far as I can see but you have something special instead of using 'fire weapon' and rolling the dice on what to hit you can use 'Aimed shot' and aim for a specific part. because you do not want an enemy mech holding a shotgun at close range. And now onto aimming you might load into the game and see percentages and be like "Ugh xcom again." and I can gladly tell you that it is not xcom! If you are point blank with someone provided they don't evade you will hit them 100% of the time! The percentages are more for how much damage you will do in what I have seen. If the enemy's EVA: (Evasion) rating is not above 50% then you have better odds then a coin flip at hitting them. My memory's terrible so that's all I've remembered in a somewhat orderly fashion, here's some more cool quirks of the game >There's friendly fire for both sides, you can get the enemy to shoot their own team mates though the ai tries to not do so, This means positioning is important both so you don't acidentally knock a friendly's head off and so the enemy shoots themselves. >Terrain and Cover matter. Hiding behind ruined temple walls and buildings do work for a singular turn, likewise if your at the top of a hill you will be able to see more and if your at the bottom of said hill you won't be able to see upwards. (This is particularly devastating if you stay in the box on a particular mission) >Losing squadmates does terrify your fellow squadmates and ones with low mental resilience witnessing friendly deaths will accumulate PTSD. I see this happening on the enemy too but it is not solidly implemented yet. >Mechs are fully customizable with a gigantic menu for all the options you could need same with swaping out parts nobody is restricted to one weapon type or body type. >There's a super indepth photo mode, which I used to create like a PTSD-esque photo >There are traits and biographies if you click on their icon in the exploration map Maybe something for a future build? I haven't tested if everyone is ambidexterous or if it is just bravo. And that's really all I can remember. Get the game it's free and its a dang blast.
